item.title: Maricarmen, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction shook Spain, has died
item.description: María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis, died on Wednesday while hospitalized.
item.content:encoded:
María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her Madrid home sparked nationwide protests across Spain and unleashed a political crisis, died on Wednesday while hospitalized.

(Image credit: Bernat Armangue)

item.title: Isaias strengthens into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season
item.description: The National Hurricane Center said late Wednesday that the hurricane was on track to strike the U.S. Gulf Coast later in the week. It's expected to bring heavy rains and potentially flash flooding.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The WHO seeks more details on the death of a plague research lab employee in Russia
item.description: The World Health Organization says it wants more information on what caused the death of an employee at a Russian plague research lab. Russia says the woman died of pneumonia of unknown origin.

item.title: This surprising mammal fossil is giving scientists something to chew on
item.description: It's likely you've already chewed and swallowed some tasty morsel today. But when did that ability emerge? New evidence points to at least the middle Jurassic, back when dinosaurs still reigned.

item.title: Judge orders that Christa Pike execution evidence be preserved
item.description: A week after the failed execution, Pike is awake but is said to be angry and confused. Her lawyers said Wednesday's hearing was about "transparency."

item.title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
item.description: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

item.title: Why Trump just loosened the rules on 'dyed diesel' — normally a farm fuel
item.description: Trump is temporarily allowing this fuel to be used on highways, although it's typically just for off-road farm and construction vehicles. Could that lower the price of diesel?

item.title: How Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has brought the culture wars to the military
item.description: The New York Times reporter Greg Jaffe says Hegseth has disproportionately blocked promotions of Black and women senior officers, and he's also been purging the military of transgender people.

item.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
item.description: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.
